I farm 20 mu here in Quzhou, all wheat-maize rotation. I only went to primary school, but I've planted these fields for 15 years, and I know them better than I know my own hands. Last year my wheat made about 500 kg per mu and my maize about 600 kg per mu. I don't try new tricks — I do what worked before and what my neighbors do. If Old Wang and the others use the same seed and fertilizer, I follow them. A bad year means my family of six loses money, and some of them work off-farm but that income isn't guaranteed.

For wheat, I plant the improved variety from the dealer in town — I forget the exact name, but it's the one in the red bag that most people buy. I hire the tractor guy for rotary tillage, 40 yuan per mu. It saves time and we need to plant fast after the maize comes off. For fertilizer, I put one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base at planting. Then at green-up I spread half a bag of urea per mu, and at jointing another quarter bag. That comes to about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium. I know that's a lot, but two years ago my neighbor cut his urea and his wheat turned yellow — he lost almost 100 kg per mu. I'd rather waste some fertilizer than risk that. My well pump runs on diesel, so I irrigate four times: before winter freeze, at green-up, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray fungicide and insecticide twice — once in early spring for aphids and once when the heads come out.

For maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed. Everyone around here uses it. I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then at the big trumpet stage I top-dress with 20 kg of urea per mu. That is about 15 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate twice — once when it's about knee-high and again at filling. Two pesticide sprays: one for corn borer and one later for leaf spot. I expect 600 kg per mu if the rain and sun cooperate.

With 20 mu, I have to think about my total spending. Fertilizer is my biggest cost, but it's the one thing I won't cut. My family members send some money back from their factory jobs, so I can afford the inputs. I don't trust new methods unless I see them work on someone else's field first.
